newsitem.title: USA: Lindsay sees FY97 revenue gains.
newsitem.headline: Lindsay sees FY97 revenue gains.

text.p: Lindsay Manufacturing Co said it may see revenue gains of 15 to 20 percent for fiscal 1997.

"Given our strong start to fiscal 1997 and expectations for continued strength in our North American and export markets, we should exceed our goal for top-line growth of five to 10 percent for the year, and may see full-year revenue gains in the range of 15 to 20 percent," the company said.

The maker of center-pivot and lateral-move irrigation equipment, said, "Second-quarter North American irrigation revenue should increase over the year-ago period as the healthy farm economy continues to have a favorable impact on demand.

"Export irrigation equipment sales should approximate fiscal 1996's second quarter as seasonal selling shifts demand from the Latin American market to the Western European market through Lindsay's third quarter."
Lindsay continued, "Full-year export irrigation equipment sales should show gains, albeit at a slower growth rate than the 79 percent achieved in fiscal 1996.
"Diversified products revenue should continue to expand modestly throughout the year."
At November 30, Lindsay said order backlog was $40.8 million, up 29 percent over the prior period.
"Repurchasing stock out of cash flow during 1997 will continue, as will our search for an acquisition representing the right fit," the company said.
